# Best slim Qi2 power banks for iPhone 17

**My pick: [Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank), $54.99**
- It's 0.34" thick and weighs 4.3 oz, with 5,000mAh and Qi2-certified 15W wireless charging.
- 9to5Mac calls it the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery and says it runs cooler than competitors ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)).
- Anker markets it for the iPhone 17 series, and it has a 30-day money-back guarantee.

**Other good options**
- **Thinnest and lightest: Baseus Picogo Air AM71 (5K).** It's 0.27" thick and 104g, and Android Central calls it the thinnest and lightest of the 2026 slim models. The catch is wireless speed of only 7.5W, so it's slower than the Anker. Prices run about $53–70 ([Android Central review](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)).
- **Slim with more capacity and speed: INIU SnapGo Air (10K, 25W Qi2.2).** It's 0.5" thick and 195g, and it gives you 10,000mAh, 25W wireless (your iPhone 17 supports this), 45W wired, and a built-in lanyard-style cable. It's about $43 at Amazon. Macworld lists it as tied for the slimmest 10K bank, though it has no kickstand ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668978/feature-best-magsafe-magnetic-portable-battery-packs-power-banks-for-iphone.html), [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)).
- **Less slim, but fast: Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10K, 25W Qi2.2, 45W wired).** It's $53.99 with code AM52 at Baseus's US store ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w), an affiliate link that earns them a commission). The results don't give its thickness, so I can't confirm it's slim.

**Which to choose**
- If you want the slimmest option that still charges at 15W, get the Anker.
- If you want one that gets you through about two full charges, get the INIU. A 5K bank typically gives roughly 60–75% of an iPhone charge, per Macworld.
- Skip the cheap Baseus at $24.99 that 9to5Mac mentions. It doesn't support Qi2, so it's limited to 7.5W.

Wireless charging works best with a MagSafe or Qi2-compatible case. Anker notes that thick or non-magnetic cases can break the connection.
